name: 30386-visionchat-gemma3-4b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine. The checkpoint is ~8.6 GB against 80 GB.
architecture: Vision-language, Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration, bf16: a SigLIP tower (image_size 896) projected into a 34-layer decoder with sliding_window 1024 and 256 prompt positions per image crop. Read off the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=8 against an engine batch ceiling of max-num-seqs 2, warmup the first 25% by completion, bounded at 1024 requests with a 900 s safety cap. Eight clients offer load; the engine runs at most two at a time, so six wait and the device stays saturated.
workload: Single-turn synthetic_text zipped with synthetic_image: per request one freshly generated 1770x1180 gradient jpeg (quality 85), exactly 15 text tokens, exactly 64 output tokens (ignore_eos). Pan-and-scan expands the one image into three 896x896 crops at 256 positions each, so a request is 816 prompt positions and 880 in total, inside the 1024 sliding window. Image resolution and pan-and-scan are load-bearing and must not be tuned away.
purpose: A visual question-answering assistant describing single high-resolution photos for eight concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# Launch config: one vision-language engine on one H100, answering a short question about one
# photograph per request. The interpreter and the hardware pin are in configs/env.yaml.

# The ungated re-upload of `google/gemma-3-4b-it` (the Gemma Terms of Use apply): same 2
# safetensors shards, 8600277880 bytes, same config.json.
model: unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it
max-model-len: 2048
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# LOAD-BEARING: pan-and-scan is why a request costs ~816 prompt positions rather than ~278.
mm-processor-kwargs: {"do_pan_and_scan": true}

limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 1}
max-num-seqs: 2
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enable-prefix-caching: false
